one_line_contribution: A number with an interval: how much an ALFWorld procedural memory bank is still worth once a reflective search optimizer has written the instruction from the *same* training episodes, measured at the bank's own re-tuned retrieval budget and game-paired against a second instruction optimized from *disjoint* episodes of the same distribution and titrated to the same no-memory accuracy, the pair of residuals being offered as an identification of episode-specific vs distribution-level absorption.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144, verified to exist) is the real threat, and the proposal concedes it: its ALFWorld ablation already reports full 59 / retrieve-only 55 / insights-only 50, i.e. each container alone recovers 85-93% of the pair built from one training pool. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202, verified; it does run GEPA and ReasoningBank as comparable self-evolution artifacts) supplies the second half. What survives is real but thin: the instruction container is a search optimizer rather than an extraction routine, k is re-tuned per instruction, and the disjoint-episode level match is an identification device I could not find published. The reason this still threatens the paper is the proposal's own pre-registered branch structure: in the E-and-not-D branch the conclusion is 'any instruction optimized on this distribution already holds the bank's value, practical conclusion unchanged', which is ExpeL's qualitative finding with a confidence interval attached. Only the E-and-D branch buys something ExpeL does not have, and by the proposal's own power analysis (D thresholded at 3pt with an MDE of 4pt) that branch is roughly a coin flip even if the hypothesis is exactly true.
strongest_objection: Every primary quantity is computed downstream of an argmax on S_dev, and the resulting selection bias is larger than the effect the primaries are trying to bound. (1) k*(I) is the k in {1,3,5,7} maximizing the paired gain of B over M0 on 75 games per k. On 75 paired games the SE of a paired gain is several points; taking the max over four values inflates g(I) at every instruction, and inflates it by *different* amounts at I0*, I_P and I'_match depending on how flat each k-curve is. The design then declares E only when |g-hat(I_P)| <= 0.9pt and tests D at a 3pt threshold - both finer than the bias just injected. (2) I'_match is itself selected: up to ten snapshots (r in {50,100,200,350,500} x 2 seeds, extendable to 750) are screened for an S_dev no-memory accuracy within 1.5pt of l_P. Selecting on a noisy dev estimate is a winner's curse: I'_match's *S_test* no-memory accuracy will regress away from l_P, so the level match that the design says makes 'headroom cancel by construction' does not hold on the test split, and row 3's D estimate re-imports the very headroom rival row 3 exists to exclude. Row 9, the null replicate, cannot catch either problem, because it re-uses the frozen k*(I_P) and a fixed instruction and therefore replicates decoding noise only. A secondary form of the same objection: matching I' to I_P on accuracy alone leaves them unmatched on rollout budget, length and prescriptiveness - the design token-matches the *scaffold* (I0_pad) and the *banks* (B', M_shuf) but never token-matches I'_match to I_P - so a positive D is equally well explained by 'the disjoint-episode instruction is shorter and less prescriptive, leaving more room for injected items' as by episode provenance.
what_would_fix_it: Take every selection off the estimation split. Use the ~700-trial reserve as a selection-only partition: tune k and pick the I' snapshot there, and report the S_test primary at a pre-fixed k, or better, drop the argmax entirely and make the primary a comparison of full k-curves (g at k in {1,3,5,7} for I0*, I_P, I'_match) so the retrieval-budget re-tuning becomes a reported surface rather than a bias-generating choice. Re-measure I'_match's no-memory accuracy on S_test and enter the realized level gap as a covariate (or an explicit adjustment) in D rather than asserting cancellation. Token- and length-match I'_match to I_P, or additionally run I' at the identical 350-rollout budget and report D at both the level-matched and budget-matched instructions. Promote two arms out of Tier 1 into Tier 0: the compiled/extraction instruction C (this is what separates novelty claim (i) from ExpeL and AutoManual, and it is currently deferred) and the coupling arm I2 optimized with memory in context, which is the configuration deployed systems actually use and the question the research track asks. Finally, either abandon the +/-3pt TOST framing, since the design admits it is declarable only at |g-hat| <= 0.9pt, and report the interval as the result, or spend the reserve to reach n = 2400 up front rather than conditionally.
missing_baseline: The ExpeL retrieve-only container - raw retrieved training trajectories in the memory slot - is absent from the entire grid. On ALFWorld that is the *stronger* of ExpeL's two containers (55 vs 50 for insights-only), so the paper measures the residual of the weaker container only and a reviewer will ask whether the residual survives when the memory slot holds demonstrations rather than distilled INSIGHT/PROCEDURE items. This also matters because the track frames the composition as 'the optimizer owns instructions, memory owns the demonstration slot', which the design never instantiates. Second omission, equally demanded: an instruction produced by a cheap non-search extraction routine (AutoManual / AutoGuide / ACE-style compiled block) from the same 300 P_train episodes, run as an instruction arm in Tier 0. Without it the claim that a *search-based* optimizer is the new thing is untested - I_type and I0_pad are controls for label knowledge and length, not for extraction. Third, deferred rather than missing: I2 (optimized with B in context) and the joint arm J sit in Tier 1, so the plan measures decomposition but not coupling.
preprint_collision: The check is above average for a proposal - dated scans, conceded collisions, a narrowly stated survivor, and four named open obligations - and I verified its factual spine rather than taking it on trust. Six searches confirmed that arXiv 2308.10144 (ExpeL), 2507.19457 (GEPA, ICLR 2026 oral), 2509.25140 (ReasoningBank), 2607.05202 (EvoAgentBench, which does compare GEPA and ReasoningBank artifacts), 2604.14585 (Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip, ICML 2026 workshop; the 49%-below-zero-shot figure on Claude Haiku is as quoted) and 2607.28272 (MemHarness; raw injection 70.1 vs 76.4 for RL without memory on ALFWorld, exactly as quoted) all exist and say what the proposal says they say. I found no preprint measuring the residual of a memory bank at a search-optimized, same-episode instruction, and none using an episode-disjoint, level-matched instruction as an identification device; on the searches I ran, the surviving contribution is not scooped. Three weaknesses in the check itself. (a) It missed adjacent 2026 work sitting on exactly this seam: arXiv 2603.21520 (Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization, memory driving the optimizer), arXiv 2606.00619 (MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs, which explicitly argues prompt-level optimization is insufficient to substitute for memory-system evolution - the direct thematic counterparty to this proposal's thesis and unaddressed by it), and arXiv 2606.23664 (MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?). None is a hard collision, but three uncited papers on the seam means the scan was not as complete as its framing implies. (b) The check reports that the abstracts of arXiv 2604.18206 and 2604.11811 were unretrievable from its node and lists them as unread; 2604.18206 (A Control Architecture for Training-Free Memory Use) was reachable from my node, so this is a node limitation being reported as a literature fact, and an unread paper about when memory should be exposed or retired is precisely the one that could pre-empt the re-tuned-budget half of the survivor. (c) The proposal's own open obligation (1), the provenance / held-out-episode crossover in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures, is the obligation that could still kill the identification claim, and it remains unrun; my six searches did not close it either. From my own memory and unverified by search: matched-performance, same-example-vs-different-example designs are standard in the memorization-versus-generalization and data-attribution literature, so 'nobody has done this' is more likely to fail on transfer-of-a-known-design grounds than on agent-memory grounds, and the proposal has not looked there. Net: no collision found, novelty not scooped, but the check has not yet earned the word 'novel' for the identification device.
